intent: Kept the ±0.03 m spread, 15 mm pitch, y = 0.05 m lead, wheels, body, and mass. Changed sensor_size from 12 mm to 16 mm to give the outer sensors more tape overlap during drift. I expect line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom to fall below 1 per run and max_error to drop clearly below 0.06 m, which would allow completions on those tracks. I expect the oval finish rate to hold or improve. Because readings will saturate differently, the Integrator may need to adjust kp and the weights. I am considering a forward move of the sensors to y = 0.06 to 0.07 if oval steering_oscillation stays above about 0.2 after this change, but I am not committing to it while line loss is still the main failure.
learning: Race 1 showed that the ±0.03 m spread fixed the oval but not s-bend or slalom. Those two tracks still lose the line at about 1 event per run with max_error at the limit, and the sensor spread alone does not explain that. Next race: if line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall and max_error drops below 0.06, the footprint was the cause. If line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at the limit, the cause is more likely controller gain or base_speed. In that case the geometry should be held and the Integrator should tune kp, kd, and base_speed. Oval steering_oscillation (0.33) remains the open question for a forward sensor move.
rationale: Race 1 (sensors at x = ±0.03 m, 12 mm footprints, y = 0.05 m) raised the score from 68.0 to 302.7. The oval track now finishes 12 of 20 trials (mean progress 0.93), so the wider spread has worked there. The s-bend and slalom tracks still end 40 of 40 trials off_track. Line_loss_events stay at 1.0 and 1.05 on those tracks, and max_error sits at the 0.06 m limit (0.0616 on s-bend, 0.0692 on slalom, which is worse than before). Oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.33, above the 0.2 threshold the Integrator set for moving the sensors forward. I took the Integrator's decision rule. Line loss is still at 1 or more while max_error is at the limit, so the sensor spread is not the main remaining cause. I am therefore holding the spread and the lead, and trying the documented next step: 16 mm footprints (sensor_size 0.016) at the same positions. This gives the outer sensors more tape overlap at the edges during drift, which is the failure the s-bend and slalom runs show. I am not moving the lead yet. The oval oscillation is a real signal, but moving the lead now would confound the footprint test, and the Integrator advised against changing the lead while line loss is the main failure. Mass, wheels, and body are unchanged, because the off-track limit is already at its floor.
